summary: Plants, restores and protects woodland in the UK. SoGive's estimate of what its tree planting (the Create Woodland project) costs per tonne of CO₂ taken up, from the 2019 annual report, rebuilt from SoGive's analysis.

source.title: Woodland Trust: SoGive rating and analysis
source.license: No licence on the page. SoGive's data terms (sogive.org/doc/getourdata.html, archived September 2019): data for charity analysis is free with attribution to SoGive; use in apps needs a licence, free for low-intensity use, on condition that users are told the source of impact assessments with a link back to SoGive. This model cites SoGive and links its page.

sections.title: Create Woodland: tree planting, 2019
sections.explainer: SoGive split the Woodland Trust's 2019 spending (£53.3m) across its three projects, sharing out the £10.4m of fundraising costs in proportion.

sections.title: Restore and Protect Woodland, 2019
sections.explainer: SoGive also costs the restoration project per tonne and calls the protection project far worse without a number. Not in SoGive's headline; our view uses them, because a donation funds all three.

sections.title: From pounds per tonne taken up to tonnes per dollar
sections.explainer: charityevals' steps after SoGive's bottom line: all three projects, since a donation to the Woodland Trust isn't restricted to planting; the survival, additionality and permanence caveats SoGive lists; pounds to dollars; and the decades over which the trees take up the carbon. The tonnes are carbon taken up by trees, not fuel left unburned, so they cut no air pollution (docs/normalization.md 2.5).

sections.title: Staff pay below market
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not the evaluator's: with credit by share of resources on, staff's pay below what they could earn elsewhere counts as an in-kind contribution and gets its share of the outcome. Off by default.

rows.explainer: SoGive assumes 5.9 kg of CO₂ a year for a tree's first 10 years and 22 kg a year for the next 90, and states the total as about 2.25 tonnes; those rates add up to 2.04 tonnes. SoGive's 2.25 is kept here, so its £2.14 reproduces; at 2.04 it would be £2.36. Every tree is assumed to survive and stand for 100 years.

rows.label: Tonnes taken up and kept, all three projects
rows.formula: (trees_planted * tonnes_per_tree * tree_survival_share + (restore_hectares * restore_additional_share + protect_hectares * protect_counterfactual_share) * tonnes_per_hectare_per_year * forest_lifespan_years) * permanence_share

rows.label: Years from the grant until the tonnes are avoided
rows.explainer: Trees take up their carbon over a century: at SoGive's rates (5.9 kg of CO₂ a year for a tree's first 10 years, 22 kg a year for the next 90) the average tonne is taken up about 54 years after planting, and a restored hectare's even uptake over 100 years averages 50. Discounting the stream year by year at 4% gives the same value as a single wait of about 40 years for planted trees (36 for restored woodland), the best guess here. Low 30: faster early growth than SoGive assumes; high 55: the undiscounted average. SoGive counts a tonne the same whenever it is taken up; the site discounts every future benefit at the discount rate under Your values, in both views. A tonne taken up then is counted like a tonne kept out of the air then: the site's climate conversion discounts its heat deaths again from that year, so no separate share of deaths "still to come" is applied. Our judgment from SoGive's rates.

rows.label: Cost per tonne taken up and kept, all three projects (£)
Our cost per tonne relative to SoGive's planting figure
rows.explainer: How much more a tonne costs once all three projects and SoGive's caveats are counted.

rows.label: Tonnes of CO₂e averted per dollar (equivalent)
rows.explainer: One over our cost per tonne in dollars (SoGive's figure times the ratio above), discounted for the wait until the trees take up the carbon, like every future benefit on the site.

rows.label: Air pollution these tonnes cut, relative to an average fossil-fuel tonne
rows.explainer: The row the site's climate conversion reads (docs/normalization.md 2.5): the air-pollution deaths each of these tonnes avoids, as a multiple of the world average behind the shared rate, 1.46 air-pollution deaths per 10,000 tonnes of CO₂ from fossil fuels (Rethink Priorities). The conversion values every tonne for its heat deaths (discounted over the decades until they come) and adds "Deaths caused by one more tonne of CO₂"'s air-pollution part times this row, at once. Here it is 0: trees taking up carbon leave the fuel burned elsewhere unchanged.

rows.label: Air-pollution deaths averted per tonne, counted directly by the evaluator (none here)
rows.explainer: A row every climate model has, which the site's conversion reads (docs/normalization.md 2.5): air-pollution deaths the evaluator counts itself, per tonne, on top of what the tonnes carry through air_pollution_weight. The evaluator counts none for this charity, so 0.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for a UK charity that both delivers services and funds others: a little under half the cost is staff. Our judgment; we haven't seen this charity's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: UK charity staff earn somewhat less than in comparable private-sector jobs. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Tonnes of CO₂ taken up per dollar donated
rows.explainer: The figure per dollar above; with credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest). The site turns these tonnes into years of healthy life through the deaths they avoid: "Deaths caused by one more tonne of CO₂", its heat part discounted over "Years until the heat deaths from a tonne of CO₂" for every tonne, and its air-pollution part, at once, times "Air pollution these tonnes cut, relative to an average fossil-fuel tonne" above. SoGive notes that tree carbon delays rather than averts emissions; in its July 2020 climate recommendations it reported academics putting 2 to more than 10 tonnes absorbed by planting as equal to one averted, which is not applied here.
